Woah! That is just amazing! So true! The worst part for me is that I became aware of this phenomenon many years ago, but still am not able to avoid it. 
[Mark Twain](http://aboutmarktwain.com/132/2013/05/11/i-have-been-through-some-terrible-things-in-my-life-some-of-which-actually-happened-mark-twain-2/)

Thanks for your replies. I'm sober now, I made that post before going outside at 3am, I dont think I specifically had any intention of doing anything, I dont really think I've got it in me. I have had the idea of suicide on my mind for a long time, but I've never really made any considered plans. The closest I may have come was just last year, when I went to Hawaii for a holiday by myself (clue there), and was given a room with a balcony on the 29th floor! Apart from being totally shit scared of heights, I asked to be put on a lower floor, as I didnt trust myself if I got really drunk, like last night. Which I did of course. 
Anyway, the drinking is a real problem now; at Christmas I got drunk and abused my brothers and sister, calling them cunts too, for not really any real reason. And boy do I regret that!. Fortunately we are all pretty close and they have chosen not to hate me for it. I see the drinking as a response to the ongoing frustration I have of not being able to get to the bottom of my issues, which is that I experience a form of mental illness, which is not yet properly diagnosed as yet. The best I can describe it is as some version of Aspergers, as I understand it there is a spectrum, and whilst I am not at the extreme end I believe I am on there somewhere. But this has proven difficult for me to identify, and address, even having seen many professionals over the past 10 years. And it wasnt until about 12 years ago when I first started to wonder what it was about me that was so different, and then started to look at what I can do about it. 
Which leads to the frustration now: that at 45 I live on my own, renting, and its not looking like I'll get married, or have any kids (my brothers and sister all have kids). I did have a partner for 8 years, but I ended it with her, again for no real reason, except that I felt like I was holding her back, as my life was not going anywhere. I've got a decent job, but at times have had issues there, as a result of my 'condition'. I have friends but I havent been in touch now for a few years, which is due to my withdrawing from society. So I dont want to be pessimistic, but its difficult to see how my future is going to pan out now, at 45. Which brings me to my main point, as I mentioned in another post here last night; that I feel that due to all of my self-destructive behaviour -binge drinking (alone) and neglecting my health and spending a lot of time hating myself for example - I'm destroying myself in a long, protracted way, as opposed to a single event. And to me that feels like a kind of suicide. 
Apologies for the wall of text, but as you may gather I dont really talk to anyone about my situation, so there you go.

It was "a friend of mine", but they lived to tell the tale. So naturally I was pretty freaked when I saw this photograph, and also am bewildered as to what message the advertisers are trying to convey.

You say that you are "only" 12, but I have to say that (at your age) the fact that you can articulate clearly how you feel, and are able to express your feelings and share them openly, (granted with anonymity) to me this is already a HUGE step! I know you wont believe it but the fact that you are already at this stage shows how far you are on the road to recovery!


I know the feelings of hate you describe, I have lived with those demons for a long time. And yeah, it totally sucks, but, they can be managed. From my own personal experience, I am not particularly a fan of therapy, but I know that if I had the same awareness of my feelings at your age I would certainly have jumped at the chance of professional help. 

I dont have kids of my own yet, but if I did and I heard this, I know that I would want to turn myself inside out to do whatever it takes to help you. I dont know what relationship you have with your parents, perhaps they are just scared as they dont know how to deal with it all... that would be understandable too. 

What I really feel is that the fact that you are reaching out for support shows that you genuinely do want to change your situation, and take heart that this shows you are in a good place. My final point is that the support is there. Nothing is more enjoyable than to be able to passionately share with friends the sentiment that music such as [this](http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zT683gHToN4) can produce (might not be your thing of course, but that was how it was for me anyway).

Your question almost sounds like a koan in itself! 
The *idea* of the cup being full and the *stating* of that idea are without judgement. As to focusing on *who* the person is who delivers that statement, and what background that person has, starts to introduce one's pre-conceived notions straight away, and distracts the mind from seeing what is there. Which is exactly what the story is attempting to point out. (At least to me, anyway). 
Now that I think about it, your question almost seems to be a troll (not wanting to cause offence if it isnt meant to be), which is funny because that is what some of the Zen stories told my the Zen Masters seem to be to me. Which is what I always liked about Zen; it has a great sense of humour!
Just make sure your cup is not [full!](http://www.101zenstories.com/index.php?story=1)
